newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daihatsu says new compact car seen boosting sales.
newsitem.headline: Daihatsu says new compact car seen boosting sales.

text.p: Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd said on Friday it would launch a new compact sport utility model in the spring which it expects to boost its domestic sales of compact cars in calendar 1997.

Daihatsu president Iichi Shingu told reporters that, helped by the launch, Daihatsu's sales of compact cars -- cars between 660 cc and 2000 cc -- would grow to 50,000 units in 1997, up 101.6 percent from the previous year.
He did not go into detail about the new model. On Thursday, Daihatsu forecast it would sell a total of 500,000 vehicles in Japan in calendar 1997, up 6.6 percent from the previous year.
Asked if the sluggish stock market would affect Japan's overall domestic car sales, Shingu told Reuters that the slump would dampen consumers' confidence.
Shingu said Daihatsu estimated that Japan's overall domestic vehicle demand, including 660 cc minivehicles, would be 7.02 million units in calendar 1997, down 0.8 percent from actual sales in 1996.
This was due to expected sluggishness in the economy due to several negative factors, including a planned rise in the consumption tax in April and falling public spending, he said.
Shingu also estimated that Japan's overall minivehicle demand would be 1.67 million units in 1997, down 1.9 percent from a year earlier.
Shingu expected the dollar-yen exchange rate to have virtually no impact on Daihatsu's exports, however, because the company's exports are yen-denominated.

Daihatsu forecast its vehicle exports would be 105,000 vehicles in 1997, up 66.4 percent from last year, with the increase fuelled largely by rising exports to Europe. Exports fell 17.5 percent in 1996.
